Which isolation rule matched first in rule order, or whether the uneditable default rule applied.
Whether the shortest configured timeout policy explains an unexpected reauthentication.

purpose.statement: Private Access isolation policy rules define when application requests are redirected to isolation; they require isolation to be enabled for the organization and an isolation profile to exist before the rule is set up.

quotes: you can create rules that define when application requests are redirected to isolation. This requires having isolation enabled for your organization and creating an isolation profile prior to setting up the isolation policy rule.

clientless-access.statement: Zscaler describes isolation policy as giving clientless access to critical applications through a containerized isolated browser so that the posture of the user's machine does not affect the applications, and as enforcing exfiltration controls that stop copy, paste, upload and download between the user's computer and the application.

quotes: Define policies to provide secure clientless access to critical applications via a containerized isolated browser on the Zscaler cloud, ensuring the posture of a user's machine doesn't affect the related applications.
Enforce data exfiltration controls by ensuring users are unable to copy, paste, upload, or download files between their computers and the applications they are accessing.

access-policy-too.statement: Besides an isolation policy, an access policy must be defined for the application to be reachable from within the isolation environment; requests not directed to isolation are reviewed against access policies.

quotes: Along with defining an isolation policy, you also need to define an access policy for the application to be accessible from within the browser isolation environment. Application requests not directed to isolation are reviewed based on access policies.

criteria-logic.statement: A request must match all the conditions within an isolation rule, and isolation rules use only the AND and OR operators.

quotes: A user's application request must match all the conditions within a policy rule.
Isolation policy rules use AND and OR operators only.

rule-order.statement: Private Access applies isolation rules in the order listed on the Isolation Policy page, and the rule order can be changed by entering a new number.

quotes: Private Access applies policy rules based on the order they are listed here. Change the rule order by clicking on the number and manually entering in a new value.

rule-action.statement: An isolation rule's action either allows or bypasses isolation.

quotes: Rule Action: Indicates if the rule is to allow or bypass isolation.

default-rule.statement: The isolation policy has a default rule that cannot be edited.

quotes: Review the default rule. This rule cannot be edited.

session-timeout.statement: Once the user is authenticated, the isolation session timeout is the minimum timeout across all configured timeout policies, after which the user must reauthenticate with Private Access to reach applications through isolation.

quotes: When the user is authenticated, the session timeout value is the minimum timeout across all configured timeout policies. After the timeout happens, the user needs to reauthenticate with Private Access to access applications via isolation.

maintenance.statement: During a Private Access maintenance period, isolation might not be available.

quotes: If Private Access is undergoing a maintenance period, isolation might not be available.

rule-action-values.statement: An isolation rule's Rule Action is Allow Isolation or Bypass Isolation, and the isolation profile field is required when the Rule Action is Allow Isolation. Isolation rules implement controls based on isolation profiles.

quotes: Rule Action: Select Allow Isolation or Bypass Isolation.
Isolation Profile: Select an isolation profile for the rule to use for allowing isolation. This field is required for creating an isolation policy that has the Rule Action set to Allow Isolation.
Isolation policy rules allow you to implement controls based on isolation profiles.

web-browser-only.statement: The Web Browser client type is required for isolation policy rules, it is the only client type available, and it is preselected for the rule.

quotes: The Web Browser client type is required for isolation policy rules, and it is the only client type available. It is preselected for the rule.

unsupported-criteria.statement: The Client Connector Posture Profiles, Client Connector Trusted Networks and Machine Groups criteria may appear in the drop-down menu, but the page says they are not supported with the Web Browser client type, which is required for isolation policies.

quotes: The Client Connector Posture Profiles, Client Connector Trusted Networks, and the Machine Groups criteria may appear in the drop-down menu, but they are not supported with Web Browser client type, which is required for isolation policies.
Rules using the Web Browser client type can not also use the Client Connector Posture Profiles, Client Connector Trusted Networks, and the Machine Groups criteria.

unsupported-criteria.conditions: This is the Configuring Isolation Policies page's wording. The same page also describes up to 10 posture condition sets, so whether posture is accepted is the disputed question in zpa.posture-profiles.policy-operand:posture-isolation and is not settled here.

rule-criteria.statement: The isolation rule page lists External IAM IdP, Applications (segments and segment groups), Chrome Enterprise Browser with an optional configured Chrome posture profile, Client Connector Posture Profiles, Client Connector Trusted Networks, Machine groups and Platforms as criteria. The SAML and SCIM Attributes criteria cannot be configured with the Cloud Connector Group criteria, and multiple Cloud Connector groups in a rule are joined by AND.

quotes: To use External IAM IdP, select the IdP from the drop-down menu.
Choose the application segments and segment groups to which this rule applies:
Enable Chrome Enterprise Browser to verify that users are accessing private applications via the Chrome Enterprise browser.
When enabled, you can also select a configured Chrome posture profile to evaluate criteria for access to private applications.
You can add up to 10 Client Connector Posture Profile condition sets to the rule.
Choose the trusted networks to which the rule applies, and click Done.
Choose the Machine groups to which this rule applies, and click Done.
Choose the platforms to which the rule applies and click Save.
The SAML and SCIM Attributes criteria type cannot be configured with the Cloud Connector Group criteria type.
If you've added multiple Cloud Connector groups to the policy rule, ZPA uses an AND Boolean operator between them.

name-characters.statement: An isolation rule name cannot contain special characters, with the exception of periods, hyphens and underscores.

quotes: Name: Enter an isolation policy name. The name cannot contain special characters, with the exception of periods (.), hyphens (-), and underscores ( _ ).

mcp-create-requires-profile.statement: The MCP server's isolation rule create tool raises an error when `action_type` is isolate and no `zpn_isolation_profile_id` is given, and creates the rule through the Python SDK's `add_isolation_rule_v2`.

quotes: if args.action_type.lower() == "isolate" and not args.zpn_isolation_profile_id:
raise ValueError("zpn_isolation_profile_id is required when action_type is 'isolate'")
client.zpa.policies.add_isolation_rule_v2(**payload)

accepted-criteria.title: Which criteria an isolation rule actually accepts
accepted-criteria.detail: The Configuring Isolation Policies page says Web Browser is the only client type and that posture, trusted network and machine group criteria are not supported with it, yet it also says a Client Connector Posture Profile must be selected before a client type, describes up to 10 posture condition sets and a Machine group criterion. Which criteria an isolation rule accepts is open; the help is one position in zpa.posture-profiles.policy-operand:posture-isolation.

isolated-but-denied.title: What the user sees when isolation policy matches but access policy denies the application
isolated-but-denied.detail: Unverified legacy statement: a user can pass the isolation policy (the session is isolated) but fail access policy, so the isolated session loads but the application inside it is denied. The help says only that an access policy is needed for the application to be accessible from within isolation.
isolated-but-denied.blocks: telling an access-policy denial from a broken isolation session

timeout-vs-idle.title: How the Private Access timeout and the container idle timeout combine
timeout-vs-idle.detail: Unverified legacy statement: Private Access isolation uses the minimum timeout across configured timeout policies in addition to the 10-minute container idle timeout, and the lower of the two wins. The sources state each separately but not how they interact.
timeout-vs-idle.blocks: predicting when a Private Access isolated session ends
